money.def: Anything people accept in exchange for goods and services. In the UK that's pounds, mostly held as numbers in bank accounts rather than notes and coins.

asset.def: Something you own that's worth money: savings, shares, a car, a house.

market.def: Anywhere buyers and sellers meet to agree a price.

interest.def: The price of using money. Savers earn it and borrowers pay it.

principal.def: The amount you start with, before any interest is added.

interest rate.def: Interest as a percentage of the principal. Nearly always quoted per year.

simple interest.def: Interest worked out only on the original principal, so it's the same every year.

compound interest.def: Interest that's added to your balance, so next time you earn interest on the interest too.

rule of 72.def: A shortcut: 72 ÷ the yearly rate ≈ how many years it takes money to double. At 6%, about 12 years.

inflation.def: The rate at which prices in general rise over time, so the same £1 buys less.

cpi.def: The Consumer Prices Index: the main UK measure of inflation, worked out by the ONS from the prices of a basket of everyday items.

nominal return.def: The return shown on your statement, before taking inflation into account.

real return.def: What you gain in spending power after inflation. Roughly the nominal rate minus inflation; exactly (1 + nominal) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1.

variable rate.def: An interest rate the bank can change at any time. Most easy-access savings accounts have one.

deflation.def: Prices in general falling over time.

bank of england.def: The UK's central bank. It sets Bank Rate and aims to keep inflation at 2%.

bank rate.def: The Bank of England's main interest rate. Savings and borrowing rates across the UK tend to follow it.

aer.def: Annual Equivalent Rate: a savings account's yearly rate including compounding, so you can compare accounts fairly.
